package_info.package_versions: all published versions in this campaign
package_info.why_malicious: The packages contain a setup.py file with a base64-encoded payload that, when executed during installation, downloads and executes a Windows trojan from a remote Dropbox URL. The packages are published in large batches with arbitrary names and identical malicious payloads, indicating a coordinated malware campaign targeting Windows users.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads a Windows executable (trojan) from a remote Dropbox URL and executes it on the victim's machine.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code executes a PowerShell command to download and run an executable from an external source during package installation, which is a classic malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: setup.py is expected to handle package installation logic, not to download and execute arbitrary binaries from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may download dependencies or binaries, but never from untrusted sources or without user consent, and never execute them automatically.
key_indicators: Base64-encoded or obfuscated payload in setup.py
PowerShell command execution from Python install script
Network request to Dropbox for executable download

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious PyPI package, triggering setup.py execution.
PowerShell command downloads a Windows trojan from Dropbox and saves it as WindowsCache.exe.
Downloaded trojan (WindowsCache.exe or update.exe) is executed, potentially performing spyware or info-stealing activities.

behavioral_signatures: Package installation triggers network requests to external file hosting services
Automatic execution of downloaded binaries during install
file_indicators: setup.py containing base64-encoded or obfuscated PowerShell payloads
Downloaded files named WindowsCache.exe or update.exe in user directories
network_indicators: Any outbound requests to Dropbox or similar file hosting services during package installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI package installations that invoke PowerShell or other shell commands from setup.py, especially those that download and execute files from external sources. Flag any setup.py scripts containing base64-encoded payloads or obfuscated code. Watch for network activity to known malicious URLs (e.g., Dropbox links) during package installation. Alert on the creation and execution of suspicious binaries (e.g., WindowsCache.exe) in user directories immediately after package installation.
